players.product: T-glass / low-Dk glass cloth for package substrates and CCL

quarterly_data.quarter: Nitto Boseki results briefing Q&A: Main Q&A, 1Q Results Briefing FY ending March 2027 (08-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): demand for T-glass remains extremely strong; the company is executing its capacity expansion plan through 2028 as scheduled and, as long as demand continues, will prioritise allocating resources to T-glass. It is deliberating further ways to expand capacity (product line replacement or major investments) against medium- to long-term demand, and says that if the opportunity is significant it will not hesitate to execute capital investments. Price revisions are not directly tied to investment decisions and would be considered when the investments allow it to increase supply volume.

quarterly_data.quarter: Nitto Boseki results briefing Q&A: Main Q&A, 1Q Results Briefing FY ending March 2027 (08-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A) on T-glass competition: because the effects of its capacity increases have not yet fully materialised, the company recognises that customers are considering low-CTE glass from other suppliers; it says its competitive advantage in the high quality required for semiconductor package substrates is unchanged, and its primary goal now is to steadily boost supply capacity to maintain market share.

quarterly_data.quarter: Nitto Boseki results briefing Q&A: Main Q&A, 1Q Results Briefing FY ending March 2027 (08-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): demand for NER-glass (low-dielectric glass) for AI servers is growing rapidly and the company plans to significantly increase its sales volume this fiscal year versus the previous year. Anticipating the transition to the second generation of low-dielectric glass, it will step up NER-glass capacity incrementally according to plan, and it currently has no plans to revise NER-glass prices during this fiscal year.

quarterly_data.quarter: Nitto Boseki results briefing Q&A: Main Q&A, 1Q Results Briefing FY ending March 2027 (08-05-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A) on the upward revision of the full-year forecast: the main factor behind the improvement in the 'Others' item versus the May operating profit forecast is price revisions for commodity products, primarily in Insulation Materials, which were not in the initial plan; it also reflects expanded sales efforts in Composite Materials and the mitigation of risks of production and sales decreases tied to supply chain disruptions from the situation in the Middle East.
